thread:
maria: Heads up — ALB in eu-west-1 started draining ~30 targets from the edge pool around 1769991200. k8s shows pods Ready=true but ALB target deregistered with `unhealthy` after healthcheck timeouts. Anyone on call? :eyes:
ryan: I see the same in our dashboard. Latency to /healthz jumped. No obvious OOM on pods. Logs show a few transient 502s from nginx.
deploy-bot: [CI/CD] rollout web-edge v2.11 -> eu-west-1 completed at 1769991288 (canary 20%).
sophie: Can you paste the ALB TG healthcheck config? interval/timeout/path?
maria: Health check config looks standard: path `/healthz` 10s interval, 5s timeout, healthy 2, unhealthy 2. Pods respond 200 but sometimes take ~3s to respond during spikes.
ryan: 3s responses with 5s timeout is tight if there are retries or transient backlog. Also ALB marks targets unhealthy after 2 consecutive fails -> fast flap.
ash (ash): fwiw, we've been seeing conntrack counts near node max on edge nodes in eu-west. SNAT exhaustion causes TCP resets which can make healthchecks fail intermittently.
maria: Pasted conntrack stats from node-12: `nf_conntrack_count=99000 nf_conntrack_max=100000` — spikes coincide with the deregistrations.
jake: Are we using ENI/NAT gateway? If NAT SNAT port exhaustion, outbound health checks from ALB origin won't be affected, but ALB->target is inbound. However target responses may fail if backend tries to call external services during /healthz (eg. contacting metadata or redis).
sophie: Good point — our /healthz was checking a downstream config service. If that call times out due to SNAT, /healthz times out. Can we make it local-only?
maria: Confirmed — readiness endpoint calls config fetch. Pushing quick patch to make healthcheck path skip downstream calls.
ryan: Also recommend increasing ALB timeout to 8s for this TG and bump unhealthy threshold to 3 to avoid 1-2 spurious drains during rollout.
ash (ash): I'll open an infra ticket to provision a small extra NAT pool and rotate nodes to clear conntrack. Also adding conntrack alert to SRE runbook.
maria: Rolling patch now, will post updates. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: [CI/CD] web-edge v2.11 patch-quick-health -> eu-west-1 started at 1769991380
jake: FYI we also observed a cluster autoscaler surge that added many short-lived pods which increases ephemeral connections — likely made conntrack worse during traffic spike.
sophie: After the patch, /healthz response median dropped from 2.9s -> 0.2s on a sample pod. Monitoring ALB state.
maria: ALB target group shows targets back to healthy after 2 min. Leaving this thread open for followups (conntrack fix + ALB threshold change).
ryan: Nice catch everyone. Add note to postmortem if we see recurrence.
ash (ash): Filed INF-4821: increase conntrack limit + NAT pool + alerting.
maria: closing once infra changes are scheduled. Thanks!
summary: ALB in eu-west-1 drained edge targets due to healthcheck timeouts. Root cause: readiness endpoint depended on downstream calls which failed under conntrack/SNAT pressure from autoscaler surge. Temporary fix: skip downstream in /healthz + ALB threshold tweak. Infra ticket opened to increase conntrack/NAT capacity.
